Recurday

Privacy

Last updated November 20, 2026.

This page says, in plain words, how Recurday treats your family's photos and notes. It matches what the app does today.

What we keep

We keep your family name, a hash of your passcode (not the passcode itself), the names and notes of your traditions, the photos you add, and the private links you share. We do not ask for an email, a phone number, or a personal account. Everyone at home uses the same family name and passcode.

Who can see a photo

Photos stay private to your family when you are logged in, and to people who have a link you sent. A family link can also add photos, so treat it like a house key. A pass-it-on invite hides photos until the other family accepts, and they cannot add photos to yours. Link previews use a generic picture, never your photos. There is no public list of families or traditions.

Shared ideas

If you use Share an idea, we keep only the words you send (a name, one line on how, and any tags you pick). We do not keep who sent it. It is not shown to anyone until a person reads it, and it may be added to Ideas in our own words, without your name.

No ads, no selling, no tracking

Recurday does not show ads, does not sell your data, and does not use analytics or tracking pixels. The only cookie is a sign-in cookie, so your family can stay logged in (about 180 days). It is httpOnly, which means other websites cannot read it.

Where it lives

Recurday runs on Cloudflare: a Worker serves the app, a D1 database holds names and notes, and private KV storage holds photos. To slow guessers, we may briefly store a record of an internet address after failed logins or too many uploads.

How to delete everything

Log in, open the calendar, and tap More. You can Save a copy first if you want to keep your photos. Then choose Delete our family, enter the passcode, and confirm. That removes your family's calendar, traditions, photos, and links. Those links will stop working. If you only want to stop one invite, use Pass it on and stop that share instead.

Recurday is a small, free, open-source project. You can open an issue on GitHub.
